territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered entities engaged in commerce, including government, or in an industry or activity affecting commerce, as defined in the bill.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Requires covered health care entities using AI/CDSS to adopt override policies, bars adverse employment actions against health care professionals who override AI/CDSS outputs, and creates whistleblower protections and enforcement. Introduced bill text.
summary.long: The Right to Override Act would require covered entities (employers, health care facilities and health plans engaged in commerce, including government) that use AI/CDSS to adopt a policy ensuring AI/CDSS outputs are not substituted for a health care professional's independent judgment and allowing timely override. Entities must inform and train staff, establish an AI/CDSS committee convening at the later of AI/CDSS adoption or 120 days after enactment, and bar sharing of override data identifying a specific professional or an inferable group, subject to exceptions. Covered entities may not take adverse employment actions against professionals who override outputs consistent with the policy requirements, or retaliate against whistleblowers. The Department of Labor may investigate and impose civil monetary penalties of up to $76,987 per violation ($769,870 for repeat violations, inflation-indexed). Individuals may file complaints and commence civil actions for damages, and state attorneys general may bring civil actions. HHS's Office for Civil Rights handles Title I complaints, including civil monetary penalties. Pre-dispute arbitration and class-action waivers are unenforceable for alleged violations. Section 303 does not protect professionals from malpractice or negligence claims, and Section 304 preserves state law and collective bargaining agreements.

notes: Bill text as introduced; the document contains no legislative history. No enabling act, amendment, repeal or transposition is stated, so no such rows are coded. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Sec. 304 disclaims preemption, so no preempts relation is coded. 'Secretary' is defined separately: HHS in Sec. 102 (title I) and Labor in Sec. 203 (title II); the Sec. 302(e) definition applies only within Sec. 302. Numbering is mixed: 'SECTION 1' and 'SEC. 2' appear in the front matter.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit or price tier was found. The dollar figures in Sec. 203(a)(3) are civil penalty maxima and those in Sec. 203(b)(2)(B)(i) are statutory damages ranges; both are enforcement content and are not coded here. Sec. 203(c) provides CPI-based adjustment of those amounts. Time periods (e.g., 120 days in Sec. 101(a)(4)(A)(ii), 1 year in Sec. 301, September 1 and October 1 in Sec. 203(c)) are procedural and belong in events.
